title: The Quiet Work of Diplomacy
text:
Diplomacy often depends on quiet negotiations that never reach the headlines. Envoys spend months refining the wording of a single clause, because a misplaced word can alter the balance of power. Such patience is rarely rewarded with public applause.

Nevertheless, the most durable agreements tend to be those in which each party believes it has gained something tangible. Where one side feels humiliated, compliance tends to erode quickly, regardless of how carefully the treaty was drafted.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, why do envoys spend months on a single clause?
options: A misplaced word can alter the balance of power
The clause must be legally long
Their governments pay them by the word

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say happens when one side feels humiliated?
What does the passage imply about public recognition and effective diplomacy?
options: Effective diplomacy often goes unrecognised by the public
Public applause is essential to every treaty
Diplomats should seek headlines in order to succeed
Public opinion has no influence on treaties

questions.text: Which conclusion best follows from the second paragraph?
options: Durable agreements depend on a perceived mutual gain

vocabulary.definition: diplomats sent to represent a government
to gradually weaken or wear away
lasting for a long time without becoming weak

paragraph_translations: Dyplomacja często opiera się na cichych negocjacjach, które nigdy nie trafiają na pierwsze strony gazet. Wysłannicy spędzają miesiące na dopracowywaniu brzmienia jednej klauzuli, ponieważ źle dobrane słowo może zmienić równowagę sił. Taka cierpliwość rzadko bywa nagradzana publicznym uznaniem.

Mimo to najtrwalsze porozumienia to zazwyczaj te, w których każda strona uważa, że zyskała coś konkretnego. Tam, gdzie jedna strona czuje się upokorzona, przestrzeganie umowy szybko słabnie, niezależnie od tego, jak starannie przygotowano traktat.
